مِنْعَبٌ An excellent, fleet horse, (S, K,) that stretches out his neck like the raven, or crow: and (or accord. to some, TA) one that follows his own way, heedless of the bridle, [app., lowering his head, and stretching out his neck,] syn. الذى يَسْطُو بِرَأْسِهِ, (K,) without any increase in the rate of his run. (TA.) ―
-b2- See نَاعِبَةٌ. ―
-b3- A stupid, or foolish, and clamourous man. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
